drills.q: Write the validation checklist a full node runs on each incoming block, in order.
drills.a: Structural: parse, size<=4M WU (BTC), Merkle root matches body, header hash meets target. Contextual: parent known+valid, height/difficulty correct for epoch, timestamps within tolerance, coinbase claims only subsidy+fees. Execution: replay all txs against state - sigs, UTXO unspent or account nonce/balance. Then fork choice.

drills.q: Two valid chains: one 5 blocks at low difficulty, one 3 blocks at high difficulty. Which wins and why?
drills.a: The heavier one wins - Bitcoin's rule is most cumulative WORK, not length. Work per block ~= expected hashes = 16^d for d leading zero hex digits; sum across the chain. A longer-but-lighter chain loses.

drills.q: Why can't an attacker cheaply rewrite blocks from last month?
drills.a: Every edit changes the block hash, invalidating descendants' prev-hash pointers AND requiring PoW redo of the whole edited suffix faster than the honest network extends the real tip. Catch-up probability from z behind is ~ (q/p)^z - exponential decay with depth.

drills.q: Half the global hashpower disappears tonight. Trace BTC's difficulty response over the next weeks.
drills.a: Block interval doubles to ~20 min immediately; retarget only fires every 2016 blocks, so ~4 weeks later actual/expected=2 -> target doubles (difficulty halves), clamped at x4. Cadence restores after the window. This lag was real during the mid-2021 China miner exit.

drills.q: Design reorg-safe deposit crediting for an exchange handling both BTC and ETH.
drills.a: BTC: value-tiered confirmations (1 small / 3 mid / 6 large), RBF-aware mempool monitoring, alarm on conflicting UTXO spends. ETH: UX reads latest slot, money moves on finalized tag (~12.8 min). Both: index by txid + (sender,nonce), idempotent ledger entries so reversals book as journal events, alert when observed reorg depth exceeds historical max.

drills.q: What exactly does assume-valid skip and why is that defensible?
drills.a: Skips ECDSA signature verification for historical blocks below a community-published hash during initial sync; structure, difficulty, and state transitions still verify fully. Defensible because any invalid old block would have been rejected live at publication; sync drops from days to hours; opt-out exists (full replay).

drills.q: Walk through the March 2013 Bitcoin fork: cause, resolution, prevention.
drills.a: Cause: v0.8 LevelDB accepted a block v0.7 BerkeleyDB rejected (lock limits) -> two valid chains ~6h. Resolution: social - major pools downgraded to v0.7 chain, orphaning ~24 blocks incl one double-spend. Prevention: cross-implementation consensus test vectors, staged activation windows, fork-detection alarms shipped in clients.

drills.q: Explain Ethereum's post-merge fork choice and finality to a backend engineer using ACID analogies.
drills.a: attn-GHOST picks head by attestation weight (latest messages); Casper FFG justifies checkpoints at 2/3 stake and finalizes on second justification (~2 epochs). latest=dirty read, safe=read-committed-ish, finalized=committed transaction no one can roll back without >=1/3 stake being slashed.

drills.q: Your CTO wants a private L1 for supplier tracking. Give the honest counter-case.
drills.a: No token means no security budget, so either one party runs everything (database with extra steps) or goodwill secures it (historically collapses: we.trade shut 2022, TradeLens wound down early 2023). Tamper-evidence without replication is trivially rewritten by the operator. Alternatives: append-only log + periodic anchoring to a public chain, or a rollup if multi-party neutrality is genuinely needed.

drills.q: Estimate the cost of a 1-hour 51% attack on Bitcoin vs ETC circa 2020 and explain the asymmetry.
drills.a: BTC: network hashrate ~700-900 EH/s of dedicated SHA-256 ASICs - not rentable on markets; attack requires billions in capex or covert pool corruption = state-level project. ETC 2020: ~250 GH/s class network where $10-50k/day of rented hashrate produced four successful reorgs (3.4k-5.3k blocks). Asymmetry = absolute hashrate + hardware specificity + rental market depth.
